resources.title: Introduction to Arts.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: Meaning of Arts
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain what Arts is
resources.activities:
Teacher: Explain what Arts is with visual aids.

Students: Mention the meaning of Arts.
resources.resources: Pictures, Real Arts, Pencils, Crayons, Drawing Books
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain meaning of Arts.

resources.title: Functional Arts.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: 1. The meaning of functional Arts. 2. Types of functional Art works: i). Woven items, e.g. mats, baskets, fans, clothing, etc. ii). Carvings, e.g. carved objects.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify types of functional Art works in the home. 2. draw diagrams of functional Art works in the home.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explain what functional Art is. 2. Show illustrations of functional Art works.

Students: 1. Identify different types of functional Art works. 2. Draw diagrams of functional Art works in the home.
resources.resources: Pictures, Real Arts, Pencils, Crayons, Drawing Books
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify functional Art works used in the home. 2. illustrate a functional Art work. 3. apply one colour to the object drawn.

resources.title: Meaning of Craft
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Definition of Craft
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able: 1. define Craft. 2. identify Craft works
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines what Craft is.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to teacher‟s explanation
resources.resources: Charts, real objects, drawing book, pencil, crayon.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: explain what craft is.

resources.title: Types of Crafts
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: Types of Crafts: 1. Embroidery: i. Table cloth ii. Hand kerchief iii. small purse. 2. Crafts in the home: :i. wall hanging ii. simple objects. 3. Drawing of crafts items:
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. name different Craft works. . 2. identify different Crafts in the home. 3. produce a coloured diagram of a Craft item.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explain types of Crafts. 2. Shows real and illustrated craft work. 3. Groups pupils to produce a coloured drawing..

Students: 1. Identify different crafts. 2. Mention crafts used in the home. 3. Draw and colour a craft works.
resources.resources: Pictures, real craft items, pencils, crayons, drawing books
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name two types of crafts. 2. identify three different crafts in the home. 3. draw and paint a craft work.

resources.title: Drawing of different craft items
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Examples of craft items: i). Beads ii). Local Mats iii). Local clay pots iv). Woven Cloths e.g  “Aso-Oke ”,  “Akwete cloth:”.  “Saki cloth”  “Parmala cloth”
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different craft items. 2. draw different craft items
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1 Shows illustrations of craft items 2. Groups pupils to draw different craft items.

Students: 1. Identify different craft items. 2. Draw different craft items. 3. Apply colour to their drawings
resources.resources: Pictures and real craft items, pencil, crayons drawing books and ruler.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify two craft items in the home 2. illustrate one craft items. 3. apply colours to their drawing.

resources.title: Children‟s Rhymes
resources.description: Theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Sub-theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Content: Children‟s rhymes
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. recite some traditional rhymes; 2. identify the lyrics of a given rhyme.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what rhymes are; 2. Finds out from the pupils the rhymes they are familiar with; 3. Plays recorded rhyme recitation; 4. Displays written rhymes on cardboard sheets; 5. Encourages individual and group recitation of rhymes.

Students: 1. Recite the traditional rhymes they already know; 2. Listen to the recorded traditional rhymes; 3. Identify rhymes in their language; 4. Copy the written rhymes in their notebooks; 5. Practice reciting the rhymes; 6. Recite rhymes in groups
resources.resources: Tape reorder and player; C.D players Phones for recording; Cardboard papers Notebooks; Pencils and cleaners.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. recite one children‟s rhymes. 2. identify the lyrics of a given rhyme.

resources.title: Role Play.
resources.description: Theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Sub-theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Content: Introduction to Role play.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify characters in a story or folk tale; 2. describe one character in the teacher‟s story or in a story told in a book.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what role play is 2. Demonstrates to pupils a character in a particular story. 3. Encourages pupils to try out roles of characters in different stories based on their observation of real life characters or animals they watches on television.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to teacher‟s explanation 2. Observe teacher‟s demonstration 3. Demonstrate and play roles in traditional stories.
resources.resources: Illustrations of characters in a story using charts, pictures, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify characters in a story. 2. play out the roles of characters in a story

resources.title: Introduction to story telling
resources.description: Theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Sub-theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Content: 1. Introduction to the art of story telling. 2. Making up a story line with any one or two of the following themes: Tolerance, Service to the nation, Truthfulness, Respect, Obedience, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to. 1. identify a story line in a story or folktale 2. create or make up a short story.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what story telling is. 2. Develops a story line idea. 3. Makes up short story around the idea. 4. Leads pupils to tell stories based on their environment, events or things they watch on television

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‟s explanation 2. Follow story line idea in teacher‟s story. 3. Make up stories led by the teacher.
resources.resources: Stories in a book; Illustrations of characters in the story; Television; Video tapes and C.Ds
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. tell the stories they created individually using any one of the outlined themes.

resources.title: Ceremonies.
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL CEREMONIES. | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL CEREMONIES. | Content: 1. Types of ceremonies: Traditional, Religious carnivals and National. 2. Examples of Ceremonies; i) Traditional- naming, marriage, fishing, durbar, etc. ii) Religious – Christmas, Sallah. iii) National – National Arts and Culture Festival, iv) Carnivals, e.g Abuja, Calabar. 3. Important values derived from ceremonies. 4. Materials associated with ceremonies, e.g. Animals, Food, Clothing.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify the different types of ceremonies; 2. give example of each type of ceremonies; 3. mention important values derived from some of the ceremonies; 4. identify materials associated with ceremonies.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the different types of Ceremonies. 2. Leads pupils to mention the examples of ceremonies 3. Explains the important values like unity, honesty, loyalty, derived from the ceremonies. 4. Guides the pupils to mention things associated with ceremonies.

Students: 1. Suggest types of Ceremonies. 2. Give examples of Ceremonies. 3. Suggest benefits derived from ceremonies. 4. Mention materials associated with specific ceremonies.
resources.resources: Pictures of Ceremonial events, Ceremonial food types, Clothing and costumes, Picture of animals, books, video films.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list the major types of Ceremonies. 2. list two Ceremonies in their locality 3. mention two items associated with specific Ceremonies.

resources.title: Body Make – up
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL MAKE - UP | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL MAKE - UP | Content: 1. Parts of the Body to be beautified. 2. Body make-ups 3. Local make – up materials for beautifying different parts of the body. .
resources.objectives: P upils should be able to: 1. mention parts of the body. 2. identify make – up used on different parts of the body, e.g. face, hands and legs. 3. beautifying parts
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Mentions parts of the body to be beautified. 2. Displays materials for making – up. 3. Guides the pupils into beautifying different parts of the body.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‟s explanation on traditional local make – up materials. 2. Describe familiar local make – up materials. 3. Apply make-up to different parts of the body.
resources.resources: Pictures of persons wearing traditional make – up materials e.g. „‟tiro‟‟, „‟tangele‟‟, camwood, „‟ndon‟‟ or Nzu (white chalk), „‟kaya and kwaliya‟‟, „‟Gazar‟‟
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify three parts of the body where make-up is applied. 2. identify two materials for body make – up. 3. apply a local make-up to any part of the body.

resources.title: Shapes and Sizes.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: 1. Drawing basic shapes of objects, e.g. rectangle, circle, triangle, square, etc. 2. Sizes of objects; Big and Small rectangles, Big and Small circles, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different shapes and sizes of objects. 2. draw shapes and sizes of objects.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Draws the basic shapes: squares, rectangles, circle, etc. 2. Displays rectangular, square and circular shaped objects of different sizes.

Students: 1. Observe different shaped objects displayed by the teacher. 2. Draw different shapes and sizes of objects..
resources.resources: Real objects of different shapes and sizes, Pencils, Drawing books, Pictures of objects showing different shapes and sizes.
resources.assessment: Pupils to draw any object of different shapes and sizes e.g. big and small circles, big and small rectangles.

resources.title: Colouring Functional Art Works.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: Colouring functional Art works.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. draw two different functional Art items. 2. apply different colours to each of the drawings.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Mentions several functional Art works. 2. Displays different art works. 3. Asks pupils to draw two functional Art works. 4. Asks pupils to colour their drawings.

Students: 1. Observe the displays by the teacher. 2. Draw two different functional Art works. 3. Apply different colours to their drawings.
resources.resources: Pictures, real functional Art works, Pencils, crayons, drawing books.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention several functional Art works. 2. draw any two of the functional Art works mentioned. 3. apply at least 3 different colours to their drawings.

resources.title: Introduction to Craft Making
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Other types of craft: i) paper craft ii) fabric craft iii) woven craft 2. Materials for craft making: i) paper ii) fabric iii) wood iv) scissors v) knife
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify more types of Craft. 2. identify materials for craft making.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains further what crafts are. 2. Explains other types of crafts. 3. Displays some materials for craft making.

Students: 1. Listen to the explanations. 2. Identify types of crafts. 3. Observe displayed materials for craft making.
resources.resources: Paper, Glue, Scissors, Coloured Pencils, Fabric Scraps, Pieces of Wood, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state the meaning of crafts. 2. identify 3 types of crafts. 3. identify some materials for making crafts.

resources.title: Designing Patterns of Basic Shapes.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Designing patterns using basic shapes. 2. Drawing basic shapes. 3. Making patterns using basic shapes.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. design simple patterns using basic shapes. 2. draw basic shapes e.g. Circles. 3. make patterns using different shapes.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists and explains basic shapes. 2. Explains what patterns are 3. Demonstrates how to make patterns.

Students: 1. Listen and draw different basic shapes. 2. Make simple patterns using basic shapes.
resources.resources: Diagrams of Basic shapes, Pencils, Colours Pencils, Eraser, Drawing books.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. make one design using basic shapes. 2. produce 3 patterns using different shapes.

resources.title: Paper Craft Making and Decorations.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS CONTD. | Sub-theme: CRAFTS CONTD. | Content: 1. Types of paper craft: i). Kite ii). Fan iii). Aeroplane 2. Uses of paper crafts. 3. Designing paper crafts 4. Making paper crafts.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify crafts made from paper. 2. state uses of paper craft. 3. draw basic shapes of paper craft, 4. make paper crafts.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. displays different paper crafts. 2. Explains the uses of paper crafts. 3. Illustrates basic shapes of paper crafts. 4. Demonstrates how to make basic paper crafts.

Students: 1. Identify paper crafts. 2. Observe illustrations of basic shapes for paper craft works. 3. Observe how to make paper crafts by folding, gluing, etc. 4. Produce a basic paper craft item.
resources.resources: Paper, Paper Gum, Glue, threads, Pencils, Scissors or Razor Blade, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify crafts 2. state uses of paper crafts. 3. make paper crafts for play or decoration.

resources.title: Pattern Making using Motifs and Colours.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS CONTD. | Sub-theme: CRAFTS CONTD. | Content: 1. Drawing of different Motifs. 2. Arranging Motifs to make simple repeat patterns. 3. Colouring Patterns.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. create simple motifs. 2. make Patterns using Motifs. 3. apply Colour to Patterns.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains What Motifs are. 2. Draws different types of Motifs. 3. Illustrates how to make simple repeat patterns.

Students: 1. Listen and observe the drawing of different types of Motifs. 2. Draw simple motifs.
resources.resources: Diagrams of different types of Motifs, Pencils, Colours, Erasers, Drawing Books.
resources.assessment: 1. draw their own motifs. 2. produce simple pattern using Motifs. 3. apply colours to the patterns.

resources.title: Traditional Songs/Folk songs.
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Content: 1. Introduction to Nigerian traditional folk songs. 2. Uses and functions of Nigerian traditional music
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify the folk songs in their languages. 2. perform a local/traditional song in unison (i.e. one part singing).
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the characteristics of folk/traditional music. 2. States the uses and functions of traditional songs. 3. Plays a Nigerian traditional/folk song of the locality in an audio tape or CD. 4. Guides the pupils to imitate the song played. 5. Write out the lyrics for the children to copy and learn

Students: 1. Listen to audio or video recorded songs of the locality. 2. Listen and sing along with the teacher. 3. Clap to the rhythm of the song. 4. Copy the Lyrics of the song.
resources.resources: Tape recorders, CD players DVD players Television Notebooks, Pencils.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify traditional songs 2. sing a specified traditional song in unison using the Lyrics and clapping to the rhythm

resources.title: Traditional Dances
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Content: 1. Traditional dances in Nigeria: (e.g. Gada, Bata, Koroso, Atilogwu, Swange, Sharo, Ekombi, Unekisin, Abigolo, Jarawa etc). 2. A specified traditional dance
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify and explain a traditional dance; 2. watch a video of a traditional dance 3. perform a specified traditional/cultur al dance.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what traditional dances are and their uses. 2. Discusses the different occasions for performing them. 3. Demonstrates a specified local dance using the basic movements. 4. Introduces drumming.

Students: 1. Identify traditional dances. 2. Imitate the dance movements as observed in the video. 3. Practices a specified dance guided by the teacher. 3. Perform in a group with musical accompaniment.
resources.resources: Musical instruments e.g. Drums, Gong, Pattlers or Shakers, Wooden drums, Clappers, Xylophones, etc Pictures of dancers performing, DVDs or VCDs Recording of dances.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify one traditional dance of their area. 2. perform a specified dance in a group.

resources.title: 3 Melodic Patterns of traditional songs.
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Content: 1. Melodic pattern of a music 2. Singing in Tonic solfa the scale of a natural key d: r: m: f: s: l: t: d: 3. Introduction of a modulator chart.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain melodic patterns. 2. Identify the melody of a specified song 3. sing a simple melody using Tonic solfa notation and clap to it
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Creates exercises using the modulator. 2. Guides the pupil on melody making. 3. Composes a simple melody using solfa notation within an octave

Students: 1. Pupils Practice random movement with the modulator. 2. Sing a melody pattern written by the teacher 3. copy a given melody.
resources.resources: - Note books - Music manuscripts - chalkboards - Modulator charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Identify the melody of a given music. 2. run the scale with the modulator. 3. Sing a song using the melodic pattern given by the teacher in solfa notation.

resources.title: Dramatization of Story telling
resources.description: Theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Sub-theme: TRADITIONAL ARTS/PERFROMANCE | Content: 1. Creation of story using identified characters 2. Dramatic elements in storytelling
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. play a role using identified characters in a story line. 2. dramatize the character of a story teller
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Introduces a popular story from the locality. 2. Highlights the major characters in the story. 3. Asks the pupils questions on the good and bad behaviours of the characters in the story. 4. Encourages and assists pupils on playing the lead role of a storyteller

Students: 1. Listen attentively and note down important points of the story 2. Answer questions about the behaviours of the characters 3. Take the lead in storytelling
resources.resources: Illustration in story books, characters in Story books Cardboard papers etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify two major characters in the story. 2. act the part of a storyteller.

resources.title: Traditional Festivals
resources.description: Theme: FESTIVAL. | Sub-theme: FESTIVAL. | Content: 1. Different traditional festivals.. Things associated with traditional festivals. 3. Important values derived from traditional festivals.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify the different traditional festivals. 2. give examples of different traditional festivals. 3. identify things associated with festivals. 4. mention important values derived from the festivals.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the different traditional festivals. 2. Gives examples of traditional festivals and where they are practiced. 3. Explains things associated with the festivals. 4. Discusses the values associated with traditional festivals.

Students: 1. Name the different traditional festivals in their locality. 2. Give examples of traditional festivals and where they are practiced. 3. Suggest some values in the festivals.
resources.resources: Costumes worn during some festivals, Pictures of some costumes, Accessories used during the festivals or pictures of the accessories..
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify two different traditional festivals. 2. list three values derived from traditional festivals.

resources.title: Introduction to Nature drawing.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: 1. Meaning of Environment. 2. Things found in the environment e.g. trees, grasses, road, animals, etc. 3. Care of the environment.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. describe their environment. 2. list the things in their environment. 3. care for their environment. 4. draw things observed within the environment.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of the environment. 2. Displays picture of a clean environment 3. Lists things found in the environment. 4. Explains how to care for the environment.

Students: 1. Listen and observe picture of a clean environment 2. Identify things found in the environment. 3. Listen to explanation on how to care for the environment.
resources.resources: Picture of the environment, trees, grasses, roads, animals Flowers, Pencils, Colours.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list things in the environment. 2. draw and colour few things found in a clean environment.

resources.title: Types of Flowering Plants.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS. | Sub-theme: ARTS. | Content: 1 Flowering plants in the environment. 2. Designing and colouring flowering plants.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify flowering plants. 2. draw and colour flowers.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Shows examples of flowers in the environment. 2. Demonstrates how to draw and colour diagram of a flower on the Board.

Students: 1. Observe diagrams, pictures, and real flowers. 2. Draw and colour a flower.
resources.resources: Diagrams, pictures, real flowers, chalks, boards, drawing books, pencils and colours.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. draw one flower of their choice. 2. colour the drawn flower.

resources.title: Use of Lines in Designs.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1Types of lines: i). ZigZag, ii). curved lines, iii). Straight lines, iv). Broken lines 2. Using lines in designs.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different types of lines. 2. use lines in simple designs.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains different types of lines with the aid of diagrams. 2. Demonstrates how to use lines in designs. 3. Displays Pupils‟ finished works.

Students: 1. Listen and observe demonstration on how to use lines in designs. 2. Draw lines to create designs.
resources.resources: Cardboard papers, markers, drawing books, pencils, colours.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify two types of lines. 2. use lines to produce 2 simple designs. 3. apply colours to the designs.

resources.title: Methods of modelling objects with clay/Plastercine
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: Modelling of objects e.g. cups, pots, etc with clay/Plastercine using: 1. Pinching method 2. Coiling method splaying of finished works.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify methods of modelling e.g. pinching and coiling 2. mould objects with clay/Plastercine
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the methods of modelling. 2. Demonstrates the: i). Pinching method. ii). Coiling method.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‟s explanation on methods of modelling. 2. Observe teacher‟s demonstration on how to use pinching and coiling methods to produce models.
resources.resources: Clay/Plastercine, wooden boards, spatulas, blunt knives, string, water, moulds.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. use any of the two methods to mould an object for display.

resources.title: Creating a drama sketch from a story or folk tale.
resources.description: Theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Sub-theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Content: 1. Play creation through scripting or improvisation with any of the following themes: Team working Patriotism, Unity, Courtesy, Dignity of labour, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. create a drama sketch from the story line of a given story or folk tale
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of play creating. 2. Explains the process of play creating. 3. Explains the concepts of scripting and improvisation. 4. Leads pupils to start a play creating process. 5. Plays a video of a play involving children as actors

Students: 1. Listen to the explanation by the teacher. 2. Participate in the play creating process. 3. Watch a video of children‟s play
resources.resources: Textbooks Notebooks Pencils Cleaners. DVDs or VCDs Television.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. create an improvised play based on the storyline of a given story with any one of the stated themes.

resources.title: Staging
resources.description: Theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Sub-theme: ENTERTAINMENT | Content: 1.Introduction to staging of a play. 2 Stages of play production.
resources.objectives: The pupils should be able to: 1. identify staging requirements of a play/drama. 2. state the different stages of a play production process.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the requirements of a play production. 2. Discusses the processes involved in play production.

Students: 1.Listen to teacher‟s explanation. 2.Identify requirements of a play production. 2. Identify the processes of staging a play.
resources.resources: Text books Note books. Chalkboard etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Identify four play staging requirements. 2. Identify three stages of a play production.

resources.title: Traditional Fabrics and Dresses.
resources.description: Theme: FASHION AND ACCESSORIES. | Sub-theme: FASHION AND ACCESSORIES. | Content: 1. Traditional Fabrics: i). “Adire” ii). “Aso-oke” iii).” Akwete” iv). “Saki” v) “Parmala” 2. Traditional Dresses: i). “Onyonyo” ii). “Buba and Iro” iii). “Sokoto”, iv). “Yar-shara” and “hula” v) “Isiagu” vi). “Babbariga/Agbada” 3. Importance of traditional dresses to the nation.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify traditional fabrics from different parts of Nigeria. 2. identify traditional Nigerian dresses. 3. draw traditional fabrics and dresses. 4. mention the importance of traditional dresses to the nation.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides the Pupils to list traditional fabrics. 2. Shows samples of traditional fabrics and dresses. 3. Explains the value and importance of traditional fabrics and dresses.

Students: 1. List traditional fabrics and dresses. 2. Observe samples of traditional fabrics and dresses on display. .
resources.resources: Samples of traditional fabrics and dresses, “ASo-oke”, “Adire”, “Akwete”, “Anger”, “Isiagu”, Dresses, “Babbariga”, “Buba” and Iro”, “Agbada”, “Sokoto” “Yar-shara and “Hula”.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify three traditional fabrics. 2. identify three traditional dresses. 3. mention two importance of traditional fabrics and dresses.

resources.title: Traditional Fashion Accessories.
resources.description: Theme: FASHION AND ACCESSORIES. | Sub-theme: FASHION AND ACCESSORIES. | Content: 1. Meaning of fashion accessories. 2. Types of traditional fashion accessories e.g. Beaded jewelleries, Corals, Combs, Walking sticks, Rattles for dancers, Shells, Cowries, Jewelleries from traditional materials. 3. Importance of traditional accessories..
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. state meaning of fashion accessories. 2. identify types of traditional fashion accessories. 3. mention the importance of traditional fashion accessories.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of fashion accessories. 2. Explains the importance of traditional fashion accessories. 3. Displays and explains different types of traditional fashion accessories.

Students: Listen and observe the display of different types of traditional fashion accessories.. etc
resources.resources: Beaded Jewelleries, Corals, Combs, Walking Sticks, Crowns, Rattles, Shells, Jewelleries from traditional materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of fashion accessories. 2. identify three traditional fashion accessories. 3. state two importance of traditional fashion accessories.
